item.title: King’s Lynn concert celebrates cultural diversity through music and dance
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn concert celebrates cultural diversity through music and dance
A sold-out concert at the King’s Lynn Masonic Centre on Sunday, October 25, showcased a blend of Indian classical and Western artistic traditions. Organised by Sursarang Arts, the "Music Beyond Borders" event featured performances ranging from Kathak and Flamenco dancing to violin and vocal collaborations. The Mayor of King’s Lynn and West Norfolk, Councillor Steve Bearshaw, was among the capacity audience.
Directors Dr Prabir Mitra and Sanjukta Mitra hosted the evening to highlight how the arts can bridge different cultures. The programme included an instrumental duet by visiting artist Pandit Pallab Bandyopadhyay and concluded with a grand finale involving all performers. The organisers hope the event will foster greater cultural appreciation across the region.

Three construction students from the College of West Anglia in Wisbech have achieved national success in the Peter Jones Foundation’s Tycoon Enterprise Competition. The enterprise also supported the charity Ryston Rachel’s Hedgehog Hotel through fundraising efforts. College staff praised the trio for their hard work and dedication, noting that the project successfully combined practical construction skills with a commitment to environmental conservation.

item.title: Calls for parking policy review after disabled shoppers face fines
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Calls for parking policy review after disabled shoppers face fines
A Dersingham resident is calling for supermarkets to offer more flexibility to disabled customers after receiving multiple parking fines in King’s Lynn. Amanda Archer, who cares for her mother, Jill Garratt, says the pair struggle to complete their shopping within standard time limits due to mobility issues.
Ms Archer received a seventy-pound charge after exceeding the ninety-minute limit at the Gaywood Aldi, and a previous sixty-pound fine at Home Bargains. Parkingeye, which manages the Aldi site, confirmed that Ms Archer’s recent fine has been cancelled following an appeal. The company stated that their system is designed to identify overstays, and they encourage motorists to submit mitigating circumstances through their formal appeals process.

item.title: King’s Lynn’s dark history explored this Halloween
item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
King’s Lynn’s dark history explored this Halloween
As Halloween approaches, King’s Lynn is being highlighted for its centuries-old history of folklore and paranormal legends. The town’s past includes the 1590 execution of Margaret Read, who was burned at the stake in the Tuesday Market Place after being convicted of witchcraft.
Beyond historical trials, the town is associated with numerous ghost stories, including reports of spectral sightings at True’s Yard Museum and the Duke’s Head Hotel. Local tales also feature a medieval exorcist’s former home and a legend involving a devil’s hoofprint left in the town’s cobbles. These stories continue to shape the town’s identity as it marks the annual celebration of Halloween on October 31.

item.description:
📰 FENLAND ANGELS RADIO | LOCAL NEWS
Marshland councillor shares budget concerns and Remembrance plans
Reform UK county councillor for Marshland North, Julian Kirk, has criticised the recent national budget. Cllr Kirk described the current system as broken, citing concerns over high taxation, rising unemployment, and unsustainable employment costs for businesses. He argued that welfare spending should be redirected towards national defence, citing the current global climate.
Looking ahead, Cllr Kirk is preparing for upcoming Remembrance commemorations. He is scheduled to lay wreaths in both King’s Lynn and Norwich to mark Armistice Day and Remembrance Sunday. Additionally, the councillor commented on potential plans for a Norfolk and Suffolk mayor in 2028, expressing scepticism regarding the promise of extra government funding.

item.description:

New gym equipment installed at Fenland leisure centres
Council-owned leisure centres in Chatteris, March, Whittlesey, and Wisbech are receiving a significant upgrade to their gym facilities. Fenland District Council has invested in new equipment, which is now being installed at the George Campbell Leisure Centre in March.
To facilitate these improvements, gyms at other sites will close for three days each. Chatteris Leisure Centre closes from November 2 to 5, followed by the Hudson Leisure Centre in Wisbech from November 9 to 12. Finally, the Manor Leisure Centre in Whittlesey will be closed from November 17 to 20. During these periods, swimming pools and fitness classes will remain open as usual. The Hudson Leisure Centre will also gain a new dedicated space for dynamic workouts.
